papers.title: Analytical Solutions of the Dunkl–Schrödinger Equation for the Manning–Rosen Potential in Higher Dimensions: Bound States and Thermodynamic Properties
papers.summary: The d-dimensional Dunkl–Schrödinger equation for the Manning–Rosen potential is solved analytically using the Greene–Aldrich approximation and a reduction to the Gauss hypergeometric equation. Closed-form bound-state energies and Jacobi-polynomial radial wave functions are obtained, recovering the standard results as $$\nu _i\rightarrow 0$$. Thermodynamic quantities are derived via a modified Bessel-function expansion and illustrated numerically for $$d = 2, 3, 4$$. We find that the Dunkl deformation systematically controls the depth and density of the bound-state spectrum: negative deformation parameters deepen the energy levels and can stabilize states that would otherwise merge into the continuum, while positive values weaken binding and dissolve near-threshold states. The heat capacity displays a Schottky-like peak whose position and amplitude depend sensitively on both the deformation parameter and the spatial dimension.
